title_en: Chen Shanhe v. Luoyang Municipal People's Government and Luoyang Zhongfang Real Estate Co., Ltd. — administrative compensation dispute
ruling_gist_en: No one shall benefit from his own wrongdoing. Where demolition parties and relevant administrative authorities illegally carry out demolition, causing the demolished person to fail to receive lawful compensation and resettlement for a long time, and housing prices rise, the demolition parties and relevant administrative authorities have an obligation to ensure that the demolished person receives fair and reasonable compensation and resettlement. Where the demolished person chooses property rights exchange for housing, and the demolition parties and relevant administrative authorities have no suitable housing for property rights exchange, they shall pay the demolished person compensation based on the market evaluation price of similar housing as of the date of the effective judgment.

full_text_en:
Chen Shanhe v. Luoyang Municipal People's Government and Luoyang Zhongfang Real Estate Co., Ltd. — administrative compensation dispute

【Ruling Summary】

"No one shall benefit from his own wrongful act." Where a demolishing party and relevant administrative organs implement demolition in violation of the law, resulting in the demolished person not receiving lawful compensation and resettlement for a prolonged period, the demolishing party and relevant administrative organs are obligated to ensure the demolished person receives fair and reasonable compensation and resettlement when housing prices rise. If the demolished person chooses to exchange for housing property rights and the demolishing party and relevant administrative organs have no suitable housing for such exchange, then the demolished person shall be paid compensation calculated based on the market appraisal price of similar housing at the time the effective judgment is rendered.

Supreme People's Court
Administrative Ruling

(2014) Xing Jian Zi No. 148

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Chen Shanhe, male, born May 24, 1958, Han ethnicity, residing in Laocheng District, Luoyang City.

Respondent for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Luoyang Municipal People's Government. Address: No. 228 Kaiyuan Avenue, Luolong District, Luoyang City.

Legal Representative: Li Liushen, Mayor of the City.

Third Party at First Instance: Luoyang Zhongfang Real Estate Co., Ltd. Address: 5th Floor, New Shanghai Commercial Building, No. 15 Qingdao Road, Jianxi District, Luoyang City.

Legal Representative: Yang Jie, Manager of the Company.

Applicant for Retrial Chen Shanhe, in connection with the administrative compensation case against Respondent for Retrial Luoyang Municipal People's Government and Third Party at First Instance Luoyang Zhongfang Real Estate Co., Ltd. (formerly China Real Estate Development Group Luoyang Real Estate Development Company, hereinafter referred to as Zhongfang Company), dissatisfied with the administrative compensation judgment of the Henan High People's Court (2005) Yu Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 00115, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court formed a panel in accordance with the law and conducted a documentary review. This case has now been concluded upon review.

The judgment of the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court (2005) Luo Xing Chu Zi No. 11 found: On April 30, 2002, Chen Shanhe purchased the disputed house from the Chanhe Branch of the Luoyang Real Estate Administration Bureau. On May 30, 2002, the Luoyang Real Estate Administration Bureau issued to Chen Shanhe the House Ownership Certificate No. Luo Shi Fang Quan Zheng (2002) Zi No. X180121. On August 19, 2002, Chen Shanhe, in accordance with the arrangements of the New Street Road Construction and Surrounding Environment Improvement Project Headquarters (hereinafter referred to as the Headquarters) established by the Luoyang Municipal People's Government, delivered his house and its appurtenances to the Headquarters. On August 20, all the houses and appurtenances within Chen Shanhe's courtyard were demolished. At the time of the forceful demolition, Chen Shanhe's household consisted of three persons. On September 14 and 17, 2002, Chen Shanhe received a total of RMB 10,000 from the Headquarters on two occasions. On December 6, 2003, the Headquarters, upon Chen Shanhe's request, temporarily lent Chen Shanhe RMB 10,000. In the relevant documents for the above three sums, the financial seal of the Third Party at First Instance, Zhongfang Company, was affixed.

The judgment of the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court (2005) Luo Xing Chu Zi No. 11 held: The Headquarters established by the Luoyang Municipal People's Government organized relevant departments to demolish Chen Shanhe's house and appurtenances, which violated statutory procedures. This forceful demolition act had been confirmed unlawful by the administrative judgment of the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court (2004) Luo Xing Chu Zi No. 11. The Luoyang Municipal People's Government should bear state compensation liability for the losses caused to Chen Shanhe's lawful rights and interests. Document No. Luo Shi Jia Zi (1997) No. 5, the "Notice on Publishing the Standards for Compensation and Resettlement for Demolition and Relocation in Luoyang City" (hereinafter referred to as the "1997 Demolition and Resettlement Compensation Standards"), does not contravene legal provisions and may be referred to by the people's court when hearing administrative compensation cases. Given that Chen Shanhe's house had already been demolished, the appraisal had lost its objective conditions, and the compensation standard could refer to the "1997 Demolition and Resettlement Compensation Standards." Chen Shanhe's house was a single-story brick-and-wood structure, classified as a commercial premises. The compensation amount was calculated as follows: (1) 55.31 square meters, compensation at RMB 620 per square meter, with an additional 100% compensation for commercial premises, totaling RMB 68,584.40; (2) Asbestos tile canopy: 32.07 square meters, compensation at RMB 100 per square meter, totaling RMB 3,207; (3) Open canopy: 12.38 square meters, compensation at RMB 20 per square meter, totaling RMB 247.60; (4) Attic: 22.68 square meters, compensation at RMB 300 per square meter, totaling RMB 6,804; (5) Three-phase motor, wires, and installation costs: RMB 2,000; (6) Moving expenses: RMB 100 per person, with Chen Shanhe's household of three persons totaling RMB 300; (7) Relocation transition expenses: The demolished buildings, open canopy, asbestos tile canopy, and attic totaled 122.44 square meters, calculated at RMB 6 per square meter for 18 months, totaling RMB 13,223.52; (8) Student transportation expenses: one student in Chen Shanhe's household, calculated at RMB 200; (9) Telephone installation fee: RMB 140. The total of the above nine items amounted to RMB 94,706.52, which the Luoyang Municipal People's Government should compensate. Chen Shanhe's claim during trial that his 104.31 square meters of property were all commercial premises and should be compensated as such lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported. In accordance with Article 58 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," it was decided that the Luoyang Municipal People's Government should pay Chen Shanhe RMB 94,706.52 as compensation for house demolition (including the RMB 20,000 already received by Chen Shanhe) within 30 days.

Both Chen Shanhe and the Luoyang Municipal People's Government were dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Henan High People's Court.

The second-instance judgment of the Henan High People's Court (2005) Yu Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 00115 found the same facts as those found in the first-instance judgment.

The second-instance judgment of the Henan High People's Court additionally found that this case was one remanded for retrial by that court. In the previously annulled administrative compensation judgment of the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court (2004) Luo Xing Chu Zi No. 12, the first-instance court identified Chen Shanhe's claims as seeking an order for the Luoyang Municipal People's Government to exchange property rights or pay economic losses of RMB 250,000. The second claim in Chen Shanhe's administrative compensation complaint was "to order the defendant to exchange property rights or compensate for losses of RMB 250,000." Chen Shanhe also provided an administrative compensation complaint dated January 10, 2004, in which the second claim was "to lawfully request property rights exchange for 104.31 square meters of commercial premises." This complaint bore the investigation archive seal of the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court.

The second-instance judgment of the Henan High People's Court held: First, regarding the method of compensation. Although Article 23 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition" provides that "the method of demolition compensation may be monetary compensation or property rights exchange for housing," this case is one of state compensation. Chen Shanhe's request for state compensation based on the unlawful damage to his property by the Luoyang Municipal People's Government can only be governed by the state compensation system, and the method of compensation can only be the statutory state compensation method. Article 25(1) of the "State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China" stipulates that "state compensation is mainly paid in the form of monetary compensation." The method of compensation in this case should be monetary compensation. Property rights exchange is a method of compensation in the demolition procedure and has no essential relationship with the method of compensation in the state compensation procedure of this case. Therefore, property rights exchange cannot be adopted as the method of compensation in this case. Accordingly, Chen Shanhe's request for property rights exchange was not supported. Second, regarding the amount of compensation. Since Chen Shanhe's house had already been demolished and Chen Shanhe did not provide other standards during the proceedings, the first-instance court's reference to the "1997 Demolition and Resettlement Compensation Standards" to determine the amount of compensation for Chen Shanhe did not contravene legal provisions and complied with the principle of fairness, and thus should be upheld. Although the Luoyang Municipal People's Government appealed the amount of compensation, the responsibility for the unlawful demolition lay with the Luoyang Municipal People's Government, and its grounds for appeal were insufficient and not supported. The Henan High People's Court decided to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Chen Shanhe applied for retrial, arguing: (1) Although the first and second instance judgments recognized the disputed house as commercial premises, when determining the value of the commercial premises, they neither referenced market prices nor commissioned an appraisal based on the applicant's submitted request for judicial appraisal. Instead, they ultimately referred to the "1997 Demolition and Resettlement Compensation Standards" to determine the demolition compensation for the disputed house and appurtenances as RMB 94,706.52, which was clearly improper. (2) At the time of demolition in 2002, a dispute arose because the relevant government departments did not recognize the disputed house as commercial premises. By the time the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court rendered its first-instance judgment in 2005, housing prices had changed dramatically. Continuing to use the prices determined by the "1997 Demolition and Resettlement Compensation Standards" would make it difficult to achieve property rights exchange in the same location. The applicant requested this Court to revoke the original first and second instance judgments and conduct a retrial in accordance with the law.

The applicant for retrial, Chen Shanhe, had no objection to the facts found in the judgment of the Henan High People's Court (2005) Yu Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 00115, and this Court confirms them.

This Court holds: The Headquarters established by the Luoyang Municipal People's Government organized relevant departments to demolish Chen Shanhe's house and appurtenances in 2002, which violated statutory procedures. This forceful demolition act had been confirmed unlawful by the administrative judgment of the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court (2004) Luo Xing Chu Zi No. 11. Therefore, the original trial court's decision that the Luoyang Municipal People's Government should bear corresponding liability for the losses caused to Chen Shanhe's lawful rights and interests by the demolition act was not improper. However, the original trial court's finding that, since Chen Shanhe's house had been demolished and appraisal had lost its objective conditions, it referred to the "1997 Demolition and Resettlement Compensation Standards" to determine the value of Chen Shanhe's house, was clearly improper.

The failure of the Luoyang Municipal People's Government and relevant functional departments to determine the nature of the disputed house as commercial premises in accordance with the law in 2002 was the main reason why the two parties failed to reach an agreement on demolition compensation and resettlement, resulting in Chen Shanhe failing to obtain compensation and resettlement in accordance with the law. The fact that Chen Shanhe has not received fair and reasonable resettlement and compensation since his house was demolished in 2002 is attributable both to the demolishing party, Zhongfang Company, failing to fulfill its compensation and resettlement obligations, and to the Luoyang Municipal People's Government and its relevant functional departments failing to act in accordance with the law. Given that housing prices have significantly increased and the demolished person has not received timely and reasonable compensation and resettlement, the first and second instance judgments ordering the Luoyang Municipal People's Government to pay Chen Shanhe only the demolition compensation and resettlement determined according to the "1997 Demolition and Resettlement Compensation Standards" were clearly unfair to Chen Shanhe.

Chen Shanhe cooperated with the demolition work and complied with the requirements of the relevant government departments. He delivered his house and appurtenances to the relevant departments for demolition without having obtained compensation and resettlement in accordance with the law. He himself was not at fault and should not bear the corresponding losses. The demolishing party, Zhongfang Company, and the Luoyang Municipal People's Government and its functional departments are obligated to ensure that Chen Shanhe receives fair and reasonable compensation and resettlement. Chen Shanhe is entitled to demand, in accordance with Articles 23 and 24 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition" effective at the time of demolition, either to carry out a property rights exchange for housing or to demand that the amount of monetary compensation be determined through market appraisal of the real estate based on factors such as the location, use, and building area of the demolished house. If the demolishing party and the Luoyang Municipal People's Government have no suitable housing for property rights exchange, then Chen Shanhe shall be paid compensation calculated based on the market appraisal price of similar housing at the time the effective judgment is rendered, to ensure Chen Shanhe's right to choose property rights exchange.

In summary, the original first and second instance judgments found the facts unclear and applied the law incorrectly, and should be corrected. In accordance with Article 63(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 63(1)(13) of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," it is ruled as follows:

1. This case is hereby directed to the Henan High People's Court to form a new panel for retrial;
2. The execution of the original judgment is suspended during the retrial.

Presiding Judge: Zhou Qiang

July 17, 2014

Court Clerk: Liu Lian
